reference.title: Barbell Narrow Stance Squat (male)
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Big breath in and brace at the top, hold it on the way down and through the bottom, breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise or at the top.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Lighter than your normal back squat; leave 2-3 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches your depth with heels down.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down, shoulder blades squeezed. Step back from the rack and set the feet about hip width apart, toes pointing nearly straight ahead.
Big breath, brace, then sit straight down: knees travel well forward over the toes, chest stays up, bar stays over the middle of the foot.
Go down until the thighs are about parallel or as deep as you can keep the heels flat and the back flat; no bounce.
Drive up through the whole foot, chest and hips rising together. Breathe out as you pass the hardest part.
Stand tall, take a new breath and brace before the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Heels lifting as the knees travel forward
mistakes.fix: Stop at the depth your ankles allow with the heels down, or use a small heel lift or lifting shoes.

mistakes.mistake: Knees caving in toward each other
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees in line with the toes; a narrow stance leaves little room, so lighten the load until they track.

mistakes.mistake: Losing balance backward at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar over mid-foot and let the knees go forward instead of pushing the hips back.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the lower back to get deeper
mistakes.fix: Stop just above the depth where the pelvis tucks under.
Squeeze the shoulder blades to build a shelf on the upper traps.

kinematics.norm: Narrower than the usual hip-to-shoulder-width stance; narrow stances shifted demand toward the knee and raised quadriceps share relative to the hip and adductors in some studies (Paoli 2009; McCaw 1999), and foot angle is usually small (Lorenzetti 2018)
To about thighs parallel; ankle dorsiflexion limits depth more in a narrow stance (Straub 2024)
Large hip flexion at depth; stance width changes hip and knee demand (Larsen 2021)
Similar to a high-bar squat at the same depth (Larsen 2021)
High bar on the upper trapezius, combined centre of mass over mid-foot (common coaching; Larsen 2021)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

cautions: Squat inside a rack with the safety arms set just below your bottom position, or with a spotter; the rack drawn here shows only the J-hooks.
The narrow stance asks a lot of the ankles and knees: build depth gradually.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Limited ankle mobility: small heel lift, or widen the stance a little.
Knee pain: reduce depth to a pain-free range.
regressions: Goblet squat with the feet close together.
Barbell full squat with a normal stance.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main movers: a narrow stance with the knees well forward loads the knee extensors heavily (Paoli 2009; McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Main movers: a narrow stance with the knees well forward loads the knee extensors heavily (Paoli 2009; McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hip out of the bottom; less adductor and glute share than a wide stance (Paoli 2009).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hip out of the bottom; less adductor and glute share than a wide stance (Paoli 2009).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hip; less active than in wide stances (Paoli 2009; McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hip; less active than in wide stances (Paoli 2009; McCaw 1999).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; length changes little.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; length changes little.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat under the bar.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat under the bar.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Control the forward travel of the knees over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Control the forward travel of the knees over the planted feet.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing stiffens the trunk under the bar.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees tracking over the feet.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees tracking over the feet.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
